claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule re-entered Earth's atmosphere on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion capsule reached speeds of approximately 25,000 mph (40,000 km/h) upon re-entering Earth's atmosphere.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket accelerated the crew to over 17,000 mph to reach orbit during the Artemis II mission.
Top speeds during the translunar injection burn reached around 24,500 mph during the Artemis II mission.
The Artemis II re-entry speed was approximately 24,000–25,000 mph.
The Artemis II re-entry represented "skip" reentry.
The Artemis II translunar injection speed was over 24,500 mph.
The Artemis II translunar injection was to break Earth's orbit.
The Artemis II orbital insertion speed was over 17,000 mph.
The Artemis II splashdown speed was slowed to 17 mph via parachutes.
The Artemis II crew hit the atmosphere at over 30 times the speed of sound during return.
Hitting the atmosphere created temperatures of around 2,760°C (5,000°F) during the Artemis II re-entry.
